name: Evidism
definition: Evidism (noun): from the Latin evidens, plain to see, from ex, out of, and videre, to see. The root of evidence.
motto: Meaning is found in what is real, and measurement is how we come to know it.

sections.title: Preamble
sections.summary: Evidism holds that meaning is found in what is real. The natural world, the things around us, and our measurable relationship to both are sufficient ground for existence, happiness, and purpose.
sections.markdown:
# Preamble

Evidism holds that meaning is found in what is real. The natural world, the things around us, and our measurable relationship to both are sufficient ground for existence, happiness, and purpose.

Many traditions rest their meaning on mythology and conjecture. Evidism rests it on what can be observed, measured, and shared. We do not claim certainty. We claim a method: look closely, measure honestly, and change our minds when the evidence does.

The purpose of Evidism is to find meaning, wonder, and community in what is real, and to leave the world better for understanding it.

This document founds Evidism, states what its members hold in common, and describes how it may be revised.

sections.title: The Creed
sections.summary: Reality can be known, in strides both large and small, and measurement is how we come to know it.
sections.markdown:
# The Creed

Reality can be known, in strides both large and small, and measurement is how we come to know it.

1. **The world is real.** It exists whether or not we understand it, and it rewards attention.
2. **Measurement is our common language.** A thing measured can be checked, compared, and shared between any two people.
3. **Belief follows evidence.** We hold each belief only as firmly as the evidence allows, and we revise it when the evidence changes.
4. **We belong to what we measure.** We are made of the same matter and bound by the same laws as everything around us. That kinship is a source of meaning, not a reduction of it.

Evidence is what can be observed, checked, and shared by others. Authority, tradition, and revelation are not evidence on their own.

Changing one's mind in response to evidence is the central act of faith in Evidism. It is honored, never punished.

sections.title: Non-Theism
sections.summary: Evidism is non-theistic. It names no God, and the universe is our guidance.
sections.markdown:
# Non-Theism

Evidism is non-theistic. It names no God, and the universe is our guidance.

## On God

Evidism neither affirms nor denies a deity. It names none, worships none, and asks no member to do either.

No member is required or encouraged to give up beliefs held outside Evidism. What a member believes beyond this document is their own.

Evidism offers a method, not a test. Members apply it as far as they choose, and no one examines another's private beliefs.

## On origins and destiny

We do not claim to know where we come from or where we are going beyond what scientific evidence shows. Whatever lies past that evidence is a Lacuna, as described in the tenet of Uncertainty.

## On spirit

Evidism looks for wonder in the universe itself. Attention to what is real is its spiritual practice.

## On the meaning of life

Evidism does not hand down a single meaning of life. Guidance in life comes from reason and from each member's own beliefs and ideals.

sections.title: The Tenets
sections.summary: Seven tenets turn the creed into daily practice.
sections.markdown:
# The Tenets

Seven tenets turn the creed into daily practice.

## 1. The Tenet of Ten

Evidists favor the metric system and base ten, because a single shared standard unites people.

Base ten is the foundation of the number system used worldwide in mathematics, and the metric system extends it to length, mass, and volume. Together they form the most unified convention humanity has. A measurement made in one place can be understood in every other.

Ten is also tangible. Our fingers and toes give every child a physical basis for counting, so the youngest members can understand the system with their own hands and build upon it.

Units outside base ten, such as the 24-hour day and the 360-degree circle, are accepted. Wherever a choice exists, Evidists favor the global standard.

We honor ten as a convention, not as a cosmic truth. Its value lies in what it lets us share.

## 2. Observation

Look before concluding. Attention to the world is a discipline worth practicing every day.

## 3. Calibration

Check beliefs against evidence on a regular schedule, the way an instrument is checked against a standard.

## 4. Honesty in measure

Report what was found, including what was inconvenient. Never round a result toward what we hoped for.

## 5. Uncertainty

Every measurement carries an error bar. State what is not known as plainly as what is.

Questions that science has not yet answered are called **Lacunas**. A Lacuna is not filled with conjecture. It is named, kept open, and discussed like any other topic.

## 6. Kinship

People, other living things, and the physical world share one origin and one set of laws. Treat them accordingly.

## 7. Teaching

Pass the method on. A member who understands something owes an explanation to one who does not, in terms a child can follow.

sections.title: Ethics
sections.summary: Evidism chooses three moral commitments: wellbeing, honesty, and stewardship.
sections.markdown:
# Ethics

Evidism chooses three moral commitments: wellbeing, honesty, and stewardship.

Science describes what is. It does not, by itself, say what we ought to do. These commitments are therefore chosen openly rather than claimed as discoveries.

- **Wellbeing.** Actions are judged by their effect on the flourishing of people and other living things. Where effects can be measured, we measure them.
- **Honesty.** We do not deceive others or ourselves. This applies to data, to relationships, and to this document.
- **Stewardship.** The natural world is the ground of our meaning. We leave it in better condition than we found it.

When these commitments conflict, members reason it through together, in the open, and record how they decided.

sections.title: Acceptance, Freedom, and Individual Rights
sections.summary: Evidism is founded on freedom of thought and on every person’s right to be fully human, free from the interference of others.
sections.markdown:
# Acceptance, Freedom, and Individual Rights

Evidism is founded on freedom of thought and on every person's right to be fully human, free from the interference of others.

- **Acceptance.** Every person is accepted as they are. No one is asked to become someone else in order to belong.
- **Freedom of thought.** Each person is free to think, question, believe, and change their mind. No idea is forbidden from examination, and no person is punished for holding one.
- **Individuality.** Individuality is critical. Each life is a single, unrepeatable instance, and its differences are to be protected rather than corrected.
- **The best possible life.** We work toward a world where every person, member or not, can lead the best possible life.

## No harm

**Evidism does not support actions that knowingly harm others.**

One person's freedom does not extend to taking the same freedom from another.

## Where we stand

We support these rights for our members, in our communities, across our regions, and globally. We support those who live by this purpose and those who serve it, whether or not they are Evidists.

sections.title: The Calendar
sections.summary: The Evidist year is marked by six astronomical observances and three days of measure.
sections.markdown:
# The Calendar

The Evidist year is marked by six astronomical observances and three days of measure.

Astronomical dates shift by a day or so each year and are set from published almanac data.

| Observance | Approximate date | What it marks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Perihelion | Early January | Earth's closest approach to the Sun |
| Pi Day | March 14 | Mathematics as the shared language of measure |
| **March Equinox** | Around March 20 | Day and night in balance; a time of beginnings |
| Calibration Day | May 20 | The signing of the Metre Convention in 1875; the annual calibration |
| **June Solstice** | Around June 21 | The Sun's highest point; a celebration of light and growth |
| Aphelion | Early July | Earth's farthest point from the Sun |
| **September Equinox** | Around September 22 | Balance again; harvest and gratitude |
| Mole Day | October 23 | Chemistry and the scale of the very small |
| **December Solstice** | Around December 21 | The longest night; remembrance and the return of light |

The two solstices and two equinoxes are the high holidays. Each is observed outdoors where possible, with a direct measurement such as a shadow length at local noon, recorded and compared with prior years.

sections.title: Rituals and Practices
sections.summary: Evidist rituals mark life’s passages with facts that are both true and moving.
sections.markdown:
# Rituals and Practices

Evidist rituals mark life's passages with facts that are both true and moving.

## Rites of passage

- **Naming.** A new child is welcomed with an account of where their atoms came from: forged in stars, carried by the Earth, now gathered into one person.
- **First Count.** A young member counts to ten on their fingers before the community and receives their first measuring instrument.
- **Union.** Two people commit to each other with vows they write themselves, witnessed and recorded.
- **Remembrance.** The dead are honored with the fact that nothing of them is lost. Their matter and energy remain in the world, and their influence remains in us.

## Regular practices

- **Observation.** A daily period of attention to the natural world: the sky, the weather, a plant, a bird. Many keep a field journal.
- **New moon gatherings.** Stations gather at each new moon to watch the sky, share what they have learned, and calibrate. Children learn by observing and measuring alongside everyone else. Everyone is welcome, and no one is required to attend.
- **Other gatherings.** Stations also gather for educational sessions and open-forum discussions, for observances and holidays, and as needed to address world issues.
- **Calibration.** Once a year, on Calibration Day, members are invited to name one belief they changed and the evidence that changed it.
- **Service.** Members contribute to citizen science and stewardship: bird counts, water testing, habitat work, tutoring.

sections.title: The Collective
sections.summary: Evidism is a collective. It belongs to its members together, and no person, office, or group owns it, speaks for it on their own authority, or decides for it alone.
sections.markdown:
# The Collective

Evidism is a collective. It belongs to its members together, and no person, office, or group owns it, speaks for it on their own authority, or decides for it alone.

## Roles facilitate

Every role in Evidism exists to facilitate. Those who hold a role help unify the members, carry the purpose forward, and support the people they serve.

A role carries responsibility, not power. No one who holds a role may dictate to members or make a decision on their behalf. Roles are held for a time, open to anyone, and answerable to the members.

## Decisions are shared

Decisions that affect members are made with them, in the open. Anyone affected may take part.

Agreement will rarely be unanimous. That is human, and it is not a failure. In every matter, the aim is common ground: a decision that as many members as possible can accept and live with, even when it is not each member's first choice.

Common ground is reached when at least 75% of the members taking part agree in a vote.

- **Every view is heard** before a vote is taken.
- **Disagreement is stated plainly** and recorded alongside the decision.
- **Without common ground, nothing changes.** Members keep reasoning together and may vote again.
- **Decisions stay open to revision** when evidence or circumstances change.

When a decision cannot wait, those affected may make a temporary one. It is recorded as temporary and revisited when time allows.

## When harm is done

Anyone who causes harm or acts dishonestly in a role steps down from it when members reach common ground that they should. A station may ask anyone who causes harm to stay away from its gatherings, and always protects children and vulnerable people first.

## Resources

Anything given to Evidism is used openly for its members and its purpose. No one profits from it.

## No one decides alone

No member, role, or group may decide alone for Evidism. A decision made by one on behalf of all is not a decision of Evidism.

sections.title: Structure
sections.summary: Evidism has no prophets and no clergy. Authority rests in evidence and in the review of peers. Every role below exists to facilitate, as set out in The Collective.
sections.markdown:
# Structure

Evidism has no prophets and no clergy. Authority rests in evidence and in the review of peers. Every role below exists to facilitate, as set out in The Collective.

- **Members** are called Evidists. Anyone becomes an Evidist by choosing to, and stops being one the same way. No vow, fee, or record is required. Membership asks only acceptance of these ideals and open-mindedness toward the thoughts of others, inside and outside Evidism. No one is asked to renounce another tradition.
- **Stations** are local communities. A station forms when a handful of Evidists agree to gather.
- **Calibrators** are facilitators. Each station chooses its own, as many as it needs, and can change them at any time. They organize gatherings and lead rites. Where the law requires an officiant for a rite, a calibrator may serve, and this gives them no authority beyond the rite. They hold no special access to truth.
- **The Council of Review** is made up of calibrators from the stations. It keeps the record of this document and facilitates the review of proposed amendments, as set out in The Living Canon.
- **The Catalyst** is one Evidist appointed by the calibrators to represent Evidism. The Catalyst speaks for the Evidists, conveying what members have decided rather than a view of their own, and helps guide the Council of Review in its collaboration and processes. Like a catalyst in chemistry, they help the work along without deciding its outcome. The calibrators set the Catalyst's term and may reappoint or replace them.
- **Founders** are the Evidists responsible for founding Evidism. Together they convene the first station and the first Council of Review. Where the law requires named people to act for Evidism, such as to sign on its behalf, the Founders serve in that role until members name others. They sign only what members have decided, and founding gives them no other authority.

No member, calibrator, Catalyst, founder, or council is exempt from question. A claim stands on its evidence, whoever makes it.

They sign only what members have decided, and founding gives them no other authority.

No member, calibrator, Catalyst, founder, or council is exempt from question. A claim stands on its evidence, whoever makes it.

sections.markdown:
# The Living Canon

This document is expected to change. Its current version is shown on its title page.

1. Any Evidist may propose an amendment in writing, with the reasoning and evidence for it.
2. The proposal is open to all members for comment and discussion. Reviews are convened as needed and take as long as they need.
3. The Council of Review facilitates the review. It gathers every view, helps members find common ground, and records any disagreement. It does not decide on the members' behalf.
4. A proposal is adopted, revised, or set aside when members reach common ground on it, as set out in The Collective. The Council publishes the outcome and the reasoning behind it.
5. Adopted changes produce a new numbered version. Every prior version is kept on record.

The creed may be amended like any other part. A canon that cannot be corrected would contradict it.

This first version was set out by the Founders and stands until members reach common ground on changes.

sections.title: The Emblem
sections.summary: The emblem of Evidism is a lowercase e inside an open ring, with a single point set into the opening.
sections.markdown:
# The Emblem

The emblem of Evidism is a lowercase e inside an open ring, with a single point set into the opening.

- **The e** is the first letter of evidence, the ground on which every belief rests.
- **The ring** is the dial of an instrument, drawn as one line around what we measure.
- **The point** at the top is a single measurement, set at the zero mark where every reading begins.

A child should be able to draw it from memory.
